_about: Labelled intents for the D-77 day clock (uro_core.timeline.clock). Each labelled row is [intent, whole days it passes]. 'fresh' was generated after the grammar's second version and measured blind (21/22 found after one later widening, so it is no longer fully held out); 'targeted' was the first held-out set and the grammar was widened against it (in-sample); 'long_run' is the 146-beat run's intents (in-sample); 'play' are generated play intents that pass no day; 'adversarial' must never pass a day. 'review' are the shapes the D-77 review found missed (each must pass exactly its days); the review's false-positive shapes joined 'adversarial'.

long_run: I walk into the Brinehouse and tell Mera that my younger brother Tomas drowned off this coast three winters ago, and that I came to learn how.

I promise Mera that I will find out what happened to the missing boats before the next new moon.
I borrow twelve silver from Mera to pay for a room, and swear that I will pay her back.
I follow the dock road to the Brinehouse, listening for the submerged bell.
I find Old Weck and ask for his advice; when he offers me a carved bone whistle to blow if the tide turns against me, I take it.
I listen as Old Weck warns me that the north quay steps flood at the third bell after midnight.
I admit to Old Weck that I have been afraid of deep water ever since Tomas died.
I thank Old Weck and head inland toward the Brinehouse, watching the dockworkers for signs of trouble.
I show Mera my father's sword, a notched old blade he named Saltbiter, and ask whether she knows a smith.
While Old Weck listens from his corner, I ask Mera quietly what she has heard about the Duke's soldiers.
I ask Mera which dockworker last saw the unmarked soldiers and where I can find them.
I head for the ropewalk and look for Nessa, keeping my hood low against the rain.
I go up to my room and sleep until morning.
I go downstairs and ask Mera what trouble has stirred on the docks.
I head toward the east sluice, keeping to the alleys while I watch what is being hauled.

I hurry after the haulers and ask where the tarred sledge is headed.
I approach the hooded figure beneath the sluice arch and demand to know who hired the haulers.
I ask the hooded figure how to reach the Brinehouse and what has gone wrong on Vel’s docks.
I wait on the seawall until nightfall to watch who comes to the old pier.
I approach the nearest unmarked figure and ask what the crews are hauling east.
I follow the eastbound crews at a discreet distance to learn who pays them.

I edge closer to the opening, listening for who is taking the purse and what the chains conceal.
I memorize the watchhouse’s location, then retreat toward Vel to find lodging and question dockworkers.
I quietly ask the dockhand what happened to Pell Rusk and the missing men.
I pay for the upstairs room, then quietly ask which dockworker still dares speak about the east sluice.
I seek out Nessa Quill along the loudest stretch of quay and cautiously tell her I want to know what happened to the dockworkers.
I tell Nessa no one sent me and ask what she saw at the east sluice.
I ask Nessa where the tide runs loudest and whether Pell Rusk left any trace there.
